title: General shutdown in Imphal Valley over the killing of three Meitei civilians

tea.why: Protesters staged a 48-hour shutdown in Imphal Valley following the ambush and killing of three Meitei civilians collecting firewood.
tea.want: Protesters demanded immediate action against armed groups, additional security, vacation of unauthorized camps, and the deputy chief minister's resignation.
tea.changed: Oct 20: Normal life was disrupted across Manipur as a 48-hour statewide general strike brought vehicular movement to a halt.

summary: A 48-hour general strike and shutdown disrupted normal life across five districts in the Imphal Valley following the deaths of three Meitei civilians in an ambush in Imphal East. Organised by the Native Peoples Committee Manipur (NPC) along with local residents, the shutdown led to deserted marketplaces, suspended public transport, and closed educational institutions. Protesters blocked roads with tyres and debris at key locations such as Khoyathong, Thangmeiband, Khurai Lamlong junction, and Tiddim Road. The demonstrations followed an emotionally charged protest where villagers and family members left bodies in front of the Chief Minister's residence, prompting security forces to deploy tear gas shells. The committee's demands include strong action against responsible armed groups, enhanced security deployment, a time-bound investigation, and the resignation of Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen.
demands: Immediate and decisive action against armed groups responsible for the attack
Identification and vacation of unauthorised armed camps near foothill areas
Additional security deployment in vulnerable areas
A transparent, time-bound investigation into the killings
Resignation of Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen
response: Security forces used tear gas shells to disperse a crowd that breached security outside the Chief Minister's residence and parked a truck carrying bodies. Police registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and individuals detained for placing bodies at the residence were later released on Monday.

deaths.text: The three Meiteis killed on Monday were collecting firewood in a forest

updates.text: A 48-hour general strike and shutdown was imposed across the Imphal Valley following the killing of three Meitei civilians.
Grieving villagers brought the bodies of victims to the Chief Minister's residence, leading to security forces firing tear gas shells.
Normal life was disrupted across Manipur with roads deserted, educational institutions shut, and transport services suspended.
